key_insight: Separating chemical and coherency strain contributions reveals that coherent interface energies reflect bonding preferences rather than lattice mismatch alone.
engineering_relevance: The database offers a reference for interpreting metallic alloy microstructures without conflating interfacial chemistry with elastic strain costs.
method: Compute 365 coherent FCC/FCC, BCC/BCC, and HCP/HCP interfaces using high-throughput DFT.
Vary superlattice thickness to separate coherency strain energy from chemical interfacial energy.
Classify results by bulk ordering tendency, interface-energy sign, and crystallographic orientation.
evidence_signal: Across 41 metallic elements and lattice mismatches up to 25%, most phase-separating systems have positive interface energies and most ordering systems have negative values; strain energy, but not interface energy, increases with mismatch.
watch_item: Quantitative comparisons depend on reference states, imposed coherent structures, and temperature; interface bonding preferences need not match bulk phase behavior.
paper_title: Energetics of Coherent Heterophase Interfaces: Separating Chemical and Strain Contributions
